result:
result: holycodex-agent also takes JSON for Intent and Assignment creation, but inline as `--input '<json>'` in argv, never from a file or stdin. holyagent takes the same JSON only on stdin. Adding an inline `--input` flag to the three JSON-reading commands closes the main gap (items 1 to 3 below).

## 1. holycodex-agent input model (working tree at 0.16.12-dev.124.1)
Entry point: `packages/agent/src/index.ts` (`runAgentBinary`, :71; `if (import.meta.main)` at :489). Help text: `packages/agent/src/help.ts`.
- **Argv shape** (`parseOptions`, :364-390): the first two words are `<command> <subcommand>`. Everything after is strict `--name value` pairs. There is no `--name=value`, no booleans, no positionals and no stdin. A duplicate option, an unknown option, or a value starting with `--` fails with `invalid_usage`. Allowed options per command are in `allowedOptions` (:392-419). Every command also accepts `--repo`, which defaults to `io.cwd`.
- **JSON handling** (:431-443): `--input` is a JSON string, decoded with `Schema.fromJsonString` and `onExcessProperty:"error"`. Failures return `invalid_input`.
- **Output** (:93-97, :104-112): stdout is one JSON line, `{schema_version:"holycodex-agent-response-1", ok:true, operation, data}`. Errors go to stderr as `{ok:false,error:{code,message,details}}`. Exit codes: 2 for `invalid_usage`/`invalid_input`, 3 for `completion_refused`, 1 otherwise. No prompts, TUI or ANSI (help.ts:5-6). The CLI itself is fully non-interactive; the interactive installer is a separate binary.
- **Help**: `-h`, `--help` or empty argv at any depth (`agentHelpRequested`, help.ts:176-178). Each help entry states the usage line, the input JSON shape and the effect (help.ts:17-168).
- **Per command**:
  - `intent create --input <json>` (:130-137). The schema is `CreateIntentInputSchema` in `packages/core/src/work-state.ts:358-365`: `{title, goal, acceptanceCriteria: string[] (min 1), planRequired?, verificationRequired?, reviewRequired?}`. A true `planRequired` is rejected (:132-135). The store generates the id and the directory `.holycodex/{slug}-{short-id}/intent.toon`, and selects the new Intent as current (help.ts:60-65).
  - `intent list` and `intent current`: no input.
  - `intent read` and `intent select`: `--intent <id|slug|dir>`.
  - `intent transition --intent --revision --state [--blocker]` (:144-150). `intent complete` and `intent abandon` take `--intent --revision`.
  - `intent evidence --input` and `intent integrate --input '{"commit":sha}'` (:151-162).
  - `assignment create --intent <ref> --revision <n> --input <json>` (:183-188). The schema is `CreateAssignmentInputSchema`, work-state.ts:451-460: `{id?, objective, owner, scope[min1], constraints?, exclusions?, dependencies?, acceptanceCriteria[min1]}`. The store writes `assignments/{id}.toon` (help.ts:115-120).
  - `assignment revise --assignment --revision --input {scope[]}`, `supersede --input {replacementId, reason, provenance}`, `start [--input {scope?}]`, `recover --input`, `result --input` (:189-257).
  - `assignment list` and `assignment read --assignment <id>`: no input.
  - `state diagnose --intent` (:259-260). `auto-reset evaluate|read|consume` (:261-301).
- **Defaults and guards it supplies**:
  - The Intent id, slug and directory are generated.
  - The new Intent is made current.
  - `--intent` is required on every Assignment command (`requiredValue(intent,"intent")`, :185 etc.). There is no implicit "current Intent" for Assignment commands.
  - `--revision` is a required positive integer for any update (`RevisionSchema` :48, `revision()` :454).
- **Why it avoids files**: the whole payload fits in one argv string, so the model never writes a draft file.

## 2. holyagent input model (/home/user/holyagent, packages/runtime/src/cli)
- **Dispatch** (`program.ts:64-114`): `parseArgs` (`args.ts:18-49`) accepts `--name value`, `--name=value`, booleans and positionals. Stdout is TOON (`program.ts:109-112`). Errors go to stderr as `error:` and `hint:` lines, with exit codes 2, 3 and 4 (`program.ts:33-34`, :116-119).
- **Where JSON comes from** (`context.ts:36-79`): the `input(schema)` / `inputBy(pick)` helpers are bound to `host.stdin` (`program.ts:52-53`). `readReport` fails with `StdinMissing` on blank stdin. The JSON is decoded with `onExcessProperty:"error"`. There is no flag, `--file` or inline source. `Call.input` is documented as "Reads stdin as JSON" (`types.ts:74-77`).
- **Per command**:
  - `intent create` (`intent.ts:61-80`): stdin `{objective, requirements?: [text]}`; `flags: {}`. The id comes from `newId` and the time from `nowIso`; the Intent is put in use (`activeIntent: id`). The slug comes from `slugOf(objective)` (`domain/intent.ts:59`). Defaults: `requirements ?? []`, revision 1, state Open.
  - `intent update` (`intent.ts:116-140`): stdin `{objective?, requirements?}` plus the `--material` flag. It acts on the Intent in use (`resolveIntent`, `intent.ts:32-47`).
  - `intent show [id]`, `list`, `use <id>`, `reopen [id]`: positionals only.
  - `intent close --reason <text> [--drop <reason>]` (`intent.ts:142-171`): flags only.
  - `assignment create` (`assignment.ts:145-164`): stdin `AssignmentInput`, which is the draft plus optional `intentId` and `intentRevision`. Shape string at :39; schema `domain/assignment.ts:75-91`. Required: `roleTask`, `objective`, `criteria` (a non-empty array of `{text, blocking, dimension}`). Defaults (`withDecodingDefaultKey`): `scope`, `constraints`, `evidence`, `ownershipPaths`, `dependencies` and `independentFrom` all default to `[]`. `completeDraft` (:47-57) fills `intentId` and `intentRevision` from `resolveIntent`, so those are implicit. Returns `{id, state}`, state Ready.
  - `assignment dispatch` (:166-205): stdin is either `{id}` (an existing Ready Assignment) or a new draft, chosen by `inputBy` (:178-180). A new draft is created and started in one step. Output is TOON plus a `prompt:` trailer (`WithTrailer`).
  - `assignment close <id> --outcome ... [--accept <rationale>] [--report-json]` (:238-312): stdin is the raw report text, or a JSON report with `--report-json`.
  - `assignment accept <id> --rationale <text> [--carry-forward] [--report]` (:314-363): `--report` reads the corrected report from stdin.
  - `assignment record <id> (--agent|--failed)`, `show <id> [--full]`, `list [--state --all --full]`: flags only.
  - `vcs pr` (`vcs/commands.ts:37`, :104, :127) takes `--body-file <f>`. `hook` commands read JSON on stdin (`hook.ts:60`).
- **Net effect**: only `intent create`, `intent update`, `assignment create`, `assignment dispatch`, `assignment close` and `assignment accept --report` need a payload, and every one of them can only get it from stdin. A heredoc or pipe works, and a file works through `< file`. There is no non-stdin, non-file way to pass a short payload.

## 3. Gaps, as minimal changes (files they would touch)
Whether "creating json files by hand" came from stdin being awkward to drive from the agent's shell tool is my hypothesis, not confirmed. The code facts above are confirmed.
1. **Inline `--input <json>` for JSON-reading commands.** In `readInput` / `readInputBy` (`cli/context.ts:59-79`), accept an inline JSON string from a flag, falling back to stdin when the flag is absent. The parsed flag value would have to reach those helpers through `callFor` (`program.ts:39-55`, `input:`/`inputBy:` at :52-53), for example via `args.flags.input`. Add `input: "string"` to the `flags` of `intent create`, `intent update`, `assignment create` and `assignment dispatch` (`cli/intent.ts:66,123`; `cli/assignment.ts:150,176`). Add the flag to the help text in `program.ts` `help()` (:23-29) and to the usage strings. This mirrors holycodex `--input` (index.ts:131, :186) and keeps strict `onExcessProperty:"error"` decoding. Touches: `cli/context.ts`, `cli/program.ts`, `cli/intent.ts`, `cli/assignment.ts`, and the tests in `packages/runtime` that cover stdin input.
2. **Flag form for simple fields (optional, higher cost).** For `intent create`, add `--objective <text>` and repeatable `--requirement <text>`. This needs a new repeatable-flag kind in `cli/args.ts` (`FlagKind`, :6), because `parseArgs` rejects only duplicates of nothing today and stores one value per name. For `assignment create` and `dispatch`, flags would be needed for `roleTask`, `objective`, `--criterion 'text|blocking|dimension'` and so on. This is bigger and has quoting risk. Item 1 gives the same benefit with less code, so I would do item 1 first.
3. **Make the "no files, no heredoc" path discoverable.** Update the `input:` strings and `notes` (`cli/intent.ts:65`, `cli/assignment.ts:39,148,170`) and the help top line (`program.ts:33`, "JSON on stdin") to say `--input <json>` or stdin. Also update the skill and command instructions that tell the root to write draft files, wherever they live under the plugin assets. I did not search those; find them with a grep for "stdin" or "draft" in the plugin.
4. **Optional holycodex parity**: a machine-readable JSON response mode (index.ts:93-97), and `--intent` and `--revision` guards on Assignment commands. holyagent already infers the Intent (`resolveIntent`, `assignment.ts:47-57`) and offers optional `intentRevision` pinning, so this is not needed for the user's request.

Additional note: the workflow and `report-json` paths (`assignment close`) are different cases. The report text is the specialist's own output, which is fine on stdin. The request only concerns the root's own Intent and Assignment drafts.
